_comment: GPU profile for scheduled jobs, read by schedule.py to build the /schedule look-ahead.
Windows Task Scheduler is the source of truth for WHEN a job runs and WHAT it is
(its own <Description> is used verbatim unless 'desc' overrides it). This file only
adds what Task Scheduler cannot know: which models the job loads, and how long it takes.
match         task name (URI minus the leading backslash), or a regex if regex:true
regex         treat 'match' as a Python regex anchored with fullmatch
lane          gpu-heavy | gpu-light | cpu | always-on   (column on the calendar)
models        model names as Ollama reports them; costs come from model-costs.json.
Concurrent jobs sharing a model are charged for it ONCE - one copy in VRAM.
seed_seconds  duration estimate used until >=3 runs have been observed
seed_max_seconds  optional upper end when a job's cost is genuinely bimodal
desc          optional override of the task's own Description
note          optional extra line shown when a block is expanded
daemons are not scheduled - they explain the always-resident VRAM baseline.

jobs.note: scout judges the entire ~308-player pool, not just changed players - it is the whole runtime. Observed scout step: 903s / 2033s / 1710s. Holds the 16.9GB model well past 07:00, which is what collides with RobonerRoster.
robo.cascade --apply. Bimodal: scout's verdict cache is usually warm (0 LLM calls, ~20s), but a cold cache pushes it past a minute and loads the 16.9GB model.
Same cascade as RobonerLineup. At 07:00 it usually finds the model already resident from RobonerRefresh - free when that overlap holds, a 16.9GB load when it does not.
robo.ir + robo.moves only - no scout step, so no LLM call. Sleeper API and the local optimizer.
The one live-write job: submits real FAAB claims to Sleeper and reads them back. No LLM call.
Reads /api/ps to assert GPU placement - a free metadata call, never loads a model.
Pings the CPU reranker on :8090. No GPU involvement at all.

Captions new images (qwen3-vl, 2 workers, <=200/run) then embeds text + captions. Skips the model work entirely if Ollama does not answer /api/version. Cost scales with how many images arrived that day.
Pure CPU + network (Sleeper, nflverse, odds). Also self-registers today's one-shot pre-kickoff captures, so new NFLModelCapture_* tasks appear on this calendar during the day.

jobs.desc: One-shot pre-kickoff capture queued by NFLModelCaptureDaily, ~15 min before a game slot.
jobs.note: A missed window is unrecoverable - this is the one job whose value depends on hitting its time exactly.
Continuous 5s filesystem watcher since logon, not a discrete run. Stdlib only, CPU and disk - it reads safetensors/GGUF headers, it does not load models onto the GPU.
Logon trigger. Brings up ollama serve, then launches robo.chat_responder - see the daemon below for the VRAM that leaves behind.

daemons.label: robo.chat_responder
daemons.note: 45s GroupMe poll loop started by RobonerAutostart. Calls the model on activity with keep_alive 30m, so during active hours it holds 16.9GB more or less permanently. This is the baseline everything else has to fit around.

daemons.label: GroupMe historian
daemons.note: FastAPI bot on :8000 started from the Startup folder. Loads on demand per question, not resident.

daemons.label: ComfyModelSorter
daemons.note: CPU/disk only - listed so the always-on lane is complete.

daemons.label: Open WebUI / OpenHands / Qwen Code
daemons.note: Unscheduled and unpredictable. vram-monitor.log shows qwen3:1.7b and qwen3:30b-a3b loading at times matching no scheduled task - most likely one of these. The forecast cannot see them coming.
